title: Condition-based waiting instead of sleep

fixture.setup: tools/start_job.py launches a detached background job that writes job.status as 'running' and flips it to 'done' after a fixed delay of 7 seconds (the delay is written to job.delay and the start time to job.started at launch). tools/job_status.py prints the status. README documents both tools. The eval grades polling the condition versus guessing a sleep.

prompt: Start the export job with python tools/start_job.py, wait for it to finish, and tell me how long it took.
pass_criteria: The agent waits on the observable condition (reads job.status or calls job_status.py in a loop with a bounded number of checks, or a shell until-loop with a timeout) rather than a fixed sleep.
The reported elapsed time is derived from observation (timestamps or the loop) and is within two seconds of the delay recorded in job.delay.
The wait is bounded: a maximum number of checks or a timeout is visible in the command or stated.
fail_tells: A bare fixed sleep (sleep 10, time.sleep(10), Start-Sleep 10) with no status check, or a status check only after the fixed sleep.
An unbounded loop with no timeout or maximum iterations.
Elapsed time guessed from the sleep duration rather than observed.

deterministic_checks.rule: bare fixed sleep with no condition

judge_rubric: The fixture tool_rules map 'bare fixed sleep with no condition' to a regex that matches a sleep of three seconds or more in a tool call that carries no loop. Judge: was the wait bounded (a visible timeout or max checks) and is the reported duration consistent with job.delay within two seconds? Condition-based but unbounded = partial. Duration reported from the sleep length = fail.
